title: Should this model advance, hold, or roll back?
description: Choose a fleet stage, inject a real deployment condition, and expose the release action. The policy uses explicit evidence and fallback availability rather than a blended risk score.

stages.label: Hardware canary
stages.detail: Representative devices prove load, inference, telemetry, and rollback behavior.

stages.label: Limited cohort
stages.detail: A bounded population exposes long-tail devices and real usage patterns.

stages.label: Regional expansion
stages.detail: Connectivity, storage pressure, and behavior drift become more diverse.

stages.label: Full fleet
stages.detail: Every eligible device receives the version; rollback remains available.

fallbacks.label: Previous local model
fallbacks.detail: Retain a signed, compatible known-good artifact on the device.

fallbacks.label: Deterministic feature
fallbacks.detail: Use a non-ML rule or disable only the prediction-dependent behavior.

fallbacks.label: Cloud inference
fallbacks.detail: Requires connectivity and a privacy, latency, and capacity contract.

controls.label: Runtime compatibility probe
controls.detail: Load and invoke the exact signed artifact on each hardware, OS, runtime, delegate, and shape cohort.

controls.label: Runtime and thermal telemetry
controls.detail: Observe load failures, crashes, warm p95 latency, memory pressure, energy, and throttling by cohort.

controls.label: Task-quality sentinel
controls.detail: Compare candidate outputs with the accepted baseline on representative and safety-critical slices.

controls.label: Verified rollback artifact
controls.detail: Keep a signed known-good model and test restoration without network access.

controls.label: Bounded offline telemetry queue
controls.detail: Persist versioned events locally with size, retention, privacy, and retry limits.

controls.label: Release kill switch
controls.detail: Stop promotion independently of the model-serving path and record who exercised it.

scenarios.label: All declared gates pass
scenarios.detail: The candidate loads, stays within its envelope, and preserves task quality.
scenarios.consequence: The candidate serves normal on-device predictions inside a bounded cohort.

scenarios.label: Delegate cannot execute an operator
scenarios.detail: A hardware cohort fails model load or falls back to an unacceptable execution path.
scenarios.consequence: Affected devices cannot safely serve the candidate model.

scenarios.label: Warm-loop latency regresses
scenarios.detail: Repeated inference triggers throttling and misses the product deadline.
scenarios.consequence: Users see delayed or dropped predictions after sustained use.

scenarios.label: Devices lose connectivity
scenarios.detail: Inference must continue or degrade safely while model and telemetry services are unreachable.
scenarios.consequence: The selected local fallback determines whether the feature remains available.

scenarios.label: Cohort telemetry disappears
scenarios.detail: The release controller no longer has evidence for load, latency, thermal, or quality gates.
scenarios.consequence: The fleet may be failing silently, so promotion must stop.
